# Products for children

## Scope

Applies when the change touches users under 13, or under 16 in the EU. Not when the service is not directed to children and knowingly collects no child's data. Neighbours: `aidd-team:privacy-by-default`, `aidd-team:accessible-ui`, `aidd-team:technical-writing`.

## Terms

- **Child**: Under 13 for COPPA; other laws differ, such as under 18 for the UK Age Appropriate Design Code.
- **Verifiable parental consent**: Consent by a method reasonably calculated to make sure it is the parent who gives it.
- **Actual knowledge**: Knowing a user is a child, which brings COPPA's duties to a general-audience service.
- **Age assurance**: Age estimation or verification, in proportion to the risk.
- **High privacy by default**: A child's settings start at their most private.

## Dated obligations

| From | Obligation | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2025-07-14 | The Commission's guidelines on the protection of minors are its yardstick for DSA Article 28(1) on every online platform accessible to minors. | S5 |
| 2025-07-24 | A UK service likely to be accessed by children has completed its children's risk assessment and protects children from harmful content. | S4 |
| 2026-04-22 | The amended COPPA Rule applies, except §312.11(d)(1), (d)(4), and (g) (safe-harbor duties, on their own dates). It requires separate parental consent for third-party disclosure, a written data retention policy, and a written information security program. | S1 |

## Invariants and missed cases

| Always true | The case a plan misses |
| --- | --- |
| No personal data from a child before consent, unless an exception applies. | An analytics or crash SDK that sends a device id at first launch. |
| A child's new feature starts at its most private setting. | A feature shipped with sharing or location on. |
| A child's data is kept only as long as its purpose needs, by a written policy. | Backups, logs, and the vendor's copy. |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | Users under 13, or under 16 in the EU, or a UK service likely to be accessed by children: the privacy and compliance dimensions, major, the privacy pool. | S1, S3, S4 |
| Specify | Age assurance, verifiable parental consent, data minimization, and defaults (private by default, no profiling, no nudges) in the Acceptance. | S1, S2 |
| Specify | The age assurance method chosen by risk (verification, estimation, or inference, stepped up where the harm is high), with its error rates. It has a fallback that is not a dead end. Content children must not reach is behind the age assurance. | S6, S4, S5 |
| Implement | No behavioral advertising, no geolocation by default, no dark pattern; plain-language notices; separate verifiable parental consent before any disclosure to third parties, targeted advertising included. | S2, S1, S5 |
| Review | Every flow of a child's data has a lawful basis and a retention limit that the published data retention policy states. The information security program covers the change. | S3, S1 |
| Ship | Consent flows and data-subject requests are the observe signals; a broken consent flow rolls back. | S1 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Consent-flow tests | nothing is collected before consent, and nothing is disclosed to a third party without its separate consent | end-to-end tests | S1 |
| Default-settings tests | private by default, no profiling, no geolocation | unit and end-to-end tests | S2 |
| Age-assurance tests | an under-age or unassured user reaches no restricted feature or content, and every assurance outcome has a path forward | end-to-end tests per age band and per assurance result (pass, fail, unsure) | S6, S4 |
| Inventory schema check | every flow of a child's data carries a lawful basis and a retention limit | a schema check over the data-flow inventory | S3 |
| SDK allow-list check | no ad or tracking SDK on the child surface | a dependency allow-list check | S1 |

- From `aidd-team:technical-writing`: Reading-level check.

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/roles.json`.
